lessons.title: Symmetry All Around Us — Anchoring the Matatu Mirror Phenomenon & Lines of Symmetry

quiz.prompt: In the matatu mirror task, learners wrote three predictions about the lorry's image in the conductor's mirror. Which set shows the three things they were asked to think about?
choices: The number of passengers, the length of the highway, and the time of day
How the image compares in size with the real lorry, where the right headlight appears and which way the image faces, and how far behind the mirror the image seems to be
The speed of the lorry, the colour of the lorry, and the price of the mirror
The number of lines of symmetry of the mirror, the weight of the lorry, and the colour of the matatu
quiz.rationale: The Predict task asked about size, orientation (headlight position and facing direction) and distance of the image behind the mirror. The other options bring in details that were not part of the predictions.
quiz.placement: Predict: three individual predictions about the lorry's image in the mirror (Think-Pair-Share)

quiz.prompt: A paper rectangle is 8 cm long and 5 cm wide (it is not a square). How many lines of symmetry does it have?
quiz.rationale: Folding a non-square rectangle in half lengthways or widthways makes the halves match, giving 2 lines. Folding along a diagonal does not make the halves match, so the diagonals are not lines of symmetry.
quiz.placement: Observe: folding the paper cut-out rectangle (non-square) and recording in the symmetry table

quiz.prompt: A pair of learners fold a paper cut-out of the capital letter F in every way they can and find that it has no lines of symmetry. Which statement gives the correct reason?
choices: F is made only of straight lines, and shapes with straight lines cannot have symmetry
F has three arms, and a figure must have an even number of arms to have symmetry
No fold line makes one half land exactly on top of the other half
F is too small to fold properly
quiz.rationale: A line of symmetry needs the two halves to match perfectly when folded. For the letter F, no fold does this, whereas the letter A matches along one vertical fold. Straight lines do not prevent symmetry: a square has 4 lines of symmetry.
quiz.placement: Observe: pairs who find that 'F' has NO lines of symmetry and explain why it differs from 'A'

quiz.prompt: A learner draws a line from one corner of a non-square rectangle to the opposite corner. The line splits the rectangle into two triangles of equal size. Is this line a line of symmetry of the rectangle?
choices: No, because a rectangle has no lines of symmetry at all
Yes, because any line that divides a shape into two equal parts is a line of symmetry
No, because when the rectangle is folded along this line the two halves do not land exactly on each other
Yes, because every line through the centre of a rectangle is a line of symmetry
quiz.rationale: A line of symmetry must divide the figure into two halves that are mirror images, so that folding makes them match exactly. The diagonal of a non-square rectangle gives two equal triangles, but they do not fold onto each other. The rectangle itself has 2 lines of symmetry.
quiz.placement: Explain: building the definition of 'line of symmetry' from the class table (probe with the rectangle diagonal)

quiz.prompt: The Kenyan flag has three horizontal bands: black at the top, red in the middle and green at the bottom, with a Maasai shield and spears in the centre. A learner draws a horizontal line through the middle of the flag. Is it a line of symmetry?
choices: Yes, because the shield is in the centre of the flag
Yes, because the three bands have the same width
No, because the flag is a rectangle and rectangles have no lines of symmetry
No, because the top half is black and the bottom half is green, so the two halves do not match
quiz.rationale: For a line of symmetry, the two halves must match as mirror images, including colour. The top half has a black band and the bottom half a green band, so they do not match.
quiz.placement: Explain: consolidation task on the Kenyan flag lines of symmetry

quiz.prompt: A rhombus is a four-sided shape with all sides equal, and it is not a square. Which lines are its lines of symmetry?
choices: The lines joining the midpoints of opposite sides
Each of its four sides
The two diagonals
The rhombus has no lines of symmetry
quiz.rationale: Folding a rhombus along either diagonal makes the two halves match, so it has 2 lines of symmetry. A common error is to choose the lines joining midpoints of opposite sides, which do not fold the halves onto each other.
quiz.placement: Observe: extension envelope (rhombus, regular hexagon and maize leaf with a small plane mirror)

quiz.prompt: At the end of Lesson 1, the class has found that a matatu mirror image is the same size as the real lorry but seems to face back at the driver. A learner writes this question on a sticky note for the Driving Question Board: 'If the image is a perfect copy, why does it look flipped?' What is the best description of this question at this point?
choices: It is answered by the fact that the lorry is moving
It was fully answered by finding lines of symmetry in the paper cut-outs
It is not yet explained, so it stays on the board for the class to investigate in later lessons
It is not a mathematics question and should be removed
quiz.rationale: Lesson 1 only opens the puzzle. The class has found lines of symmetry but has not yet explained why a perfect copy can look flipped, so the question stays on the board.
quiz.placement: Driving Question Board: sticky-note questions and observations about the matatu mirror

lessons.title: Same Shape, Same Size — Direct and Opposite Congruence with Paper Cut-outs

quiz.prompt: Two shapes are described as congruent. Which statement best explains what congruent means?
choices: They have the same shape, but one may be bigger than the other.
They have the same shape and the same size.
They are in the same position on the desk and face the same direction.
They have the same area, even if their shapes are different, such as a 4 cm by 3 cm rectangle and a 6 cm by 2 cm rectangle.
quiz.rationale: Congruent shapes match in both shape and size. Position and direction can differ, and equal area alone is not enough.
quiz.placement: Predict: Lake Victoria reflection predictions, question 3 ('exactly the same shape and size')

quiz.prompt: A learner folds a sheet of paper, draws a lopsided letter F (no line of symmetry) and cuts through both layers to get pieces A and B. With a pencil dot facing up on both pieces, piece B slides and turns onto piece A and fits exactly. The learner then turns piece B over (dot face down). What happens?
choices: It becomes smaller than piece A, so it cannot fit.
It still fits exactly on piece A without being turned back over, because the pieces are identical.
It becomes a mirror copy of piece A and does not fit unless it is flipped back over.
It fits only if piece A is also cut again to a new shape.
quiz.rationale: Flipping a shape with no line of symmetry gives its mirror copy. The size and shape stay the same, but the piece will not fit until it is flipped back.
quiz.placement: Observe, Task 1: lopsided shape cut from folded paper, testing with the dot up and then flipped

quiz.prompt: A learner cuts an isosceles triangle from folded paper to get two identical pieces. Piece B is turned over (dot face down). Why does it still fit exactly on piece A without being turned back?
choices: Because turning a piece over never changes how it looks, for any shape.
Because the two pieces are different sizes.
Because the triangle has a line of symmetry, so its flipped copy looks the same as the original.
Because the triangle has three sides.
quiz.rationale: A shape with a line of symmetry looks the same when flipped, so the flipped copy fits too. This does not happen for shapes with no line of symmetry.
quiz.placement: Observe, Task 2: shape that HAS a line of symmetry (isosceles triangle or rectangle)

quiz.prompt: A cook uses the same circular cutter to cut two chapatis. The two circles have the same radius. Which kind of congruence do the two circles have?
choices: Neither, because circles have no corners.
Opposite congruence only, because every pair of copies is a mirror pair.
Both direct and opposite congruence, because a circle has lines of symmetry and so looks the same when flipped.
Direct congruence only, because circles can never be flipped.
quiz.rationale: One circle fits on the other by sliding, and it also fits after being flipped, because a circle has lines of symmetry.
quiz.placement: Explain: classifying three pairs on the board, (iii) two circles of the same radius

quiz.prompt: Two identical lopsided triangles lie on a desk in the same orientation (neither is flipped). One can be slid onto the other. What kind of congruence is this?
choices: Opposite congruence, because the triangles are separate.
They are not congruent, because they are in different places.
Opposite congruence, because the triangles have no line of symmetry.
Direct congruence, because one fits on the other by sliding and/or turning with no flip.
quiz.rationale: If one shape fits on the other by sliding and/or turning only, with no flip, the congruence is direct. Position on the desk does not matter.
quiz.placement: Explain: classifying three pairs on the board, (i) two identical lopsided triangles in the same orientation

quiz.prompt: A teacher holds up a brick-shaped box whose length, width and height are all different. How many planes of symmetry does it have, where each plane cuts the box into two mirror-image halves?
quiz.rationale: There is one plane through the middle of the box parallel to each pair of faces, giving 3 planes. A plane parallel to one pair of faces does not make mirror halves along a diagonal, so there are no others.
quiz.placement: Explain: planes of symmetry of a box-shaped object (matchbox or brick-shaped box with three different edge lengths)

quiz.prompt: The hills of Homa Bay are reflected in the still water of Lake Victoria. The reflection has the same shape and size as the hills, but it is upside down, like a mirror copy. Which kind of congruence would you expect between the hills and their reflection?
choices: Direct congruence, because the reflection is the same size.
Opposite congruence, because a mirror copy would need to be flipped over to fit the original.
Direct congruence, because the reflection can be slid up onto the hills.
Neither, because a reflection is only a picture.
quiz.rationale: A mirror copy has the same shape and size but is flipped, so the expected congruence is opposite. The lesson treats this as a hypothesis to be tested in later lessons.
quiz.placement: Model Building: hypothesis box 'the image is a mirror copy of the object, so we think it is OPPOSITE congruent'

lessons.title: Reflection on the Cartesian Plane — Plotting Object and Image Coordinates

quiz.prompt: A point P(3, 2) is marked on a Cartesian grid. The mirror line is the y-axis (x = 0). What are the coordinates of the image P′?
quiz.rationale: P is 3 squares to the right of the y-axis, so P′ is 3 squares to the left at the same height. This gives (−3, 2): only the x-coordinate changes sign.
quiz.placement: Predict: write the coordinates of P's mirror image in the y-axis

quiz.prompt: When reflecting a vertex in a mirror line on the Cartesian grid, you draw a line from the vertex to the mirror line using a set-square. At what angle should this line meet the mirror line?
choices: It can be any angle, as long as the counts of squares are equal
quiz.rationale: The line from an object point to the mirror line must be perpendicular (90°). The image point is then found by counting the same distance along that perpendicular on the other side.
quiz.placement: Observe: Reflection Investigation Worksheet, drawing perpendiculars with a ruler and set-square

quiz.prompt: A lorry-shaped quadrilateral ABCD has vertices A(1, 1), B(4, 1), C(4, 3) and D(1, 3). It is reflected in the y-axis (x = 0). What are the coordinates of C′?
quiz.rationale: C is 4 squares to the right of the y-axis, so C′ is 4 squares to the left at the same height. The rule (a, b) → (−a, b) gives C′(−4, 3).
quiz.placement: Observe: grid (i), reflecting quadrilateral ABCD in the y-axis (x = 0)

quiz.prompt: The point C(4, 3) is reflected in the line y = −x. What are the coordinates of C′?
quiz.rationale: The rule for reflection in y = −x is (a, b) → (−b, −a). So (4, 3) → (−3, −4).
quiz.placement: Observe: grid (iv), reflecting vertices A and C in y = −x, and completing the Coordinate Rule Table

quiz.prompt: A point K(−2, 5) is reflected in the line y = x. What are the coordinates of K′?
quiz.rationale: Reflection in y = x swaps the coordinates: (a, b) → (b, a). So (−2, 5) → (5, −2). Writing (−b, −a) is the common mix-up with y = −x.
quiz.placement: Explain: Reflection Rules Reference Card, consolidation question Q1

quiz.prompt: After reflection in the x-axis (y = 0), the image of a point M is M′(4, −3). What are the coordinates of the original point M?
quiz.rationale: Reflecting M′ back in the same mirror line returns the original point. The rule (a, b) → (a, −b) gives M(4, 3).
quiz.placement: Explain: Reflection Rules Reference Card, consolidation question Q2

quiz.prompt: Side CD of the lorry quadrilateral has C(4, 3) and D(1, 3), so its length is 3 units. After reflection in the y-axis, the image points are C′(−4, 3) and D′(−1, 3). What is the length of C′D′?
choices: 3 units
1 unit
4 units
5 units
quiz.rationale: C′ and D′ are on the same horizontal line, so the distance is |−4 − (−1)| = 3 units. The reflection rule preserves distances, which is why the lorry's image in the matatu mirror is the same size as the lorry.
quiz.placement: Explain: whole-class discussion on why the lorry image in the matatu mirror is the same size as the real lorry

quiz.prompt: A flat rear-view mirror is modelled as the vertical line x = 3 on a grid. A point on the lorry is at (5, 2). What are the coordinates of its image?
quiz.rationale: The point is 5 − 3 = 2 squares to the right of the mirror line, so the image is 2 squares to the left of it, at x = 1. The height stays the same, so the image is (1, 2), from (a, b) → (2k − a, b) = (6 − 5, 2).
quiz.placement: Model: Cartesian overlay on the cumulative model, modelling a flat rear-view mirror as a vertical line x = k

lessons.title: Properties of Reflection — Discovering the Four Rules of the Mirror Line

quiz.prompt: A plane mirror forms an image of a lorry that is 8 m long. How long is the image of the lorry?
choices: 8 m, because the image is the same size as the object
It depends on how far the lorry is from the mirror
4 m, because images in a mirror are smaller
16 m, because the image is behind the mirror as well
quiz.rationale: Property I: a plane mirror image is the same size as the object, so the image is also 8 m long. Objects that are far away only look smaller to the eye. The image does not actually change size.
quiz.placement: Predict: written prediction prompt (1) on the size of the lorry's image

quiz.prompt: In the matatu arrow investigation, a group measures the distance from point A to the mirror line and gets 35 mm. What distance should they measure from the image point A' to the mirror line?
choices: 17 mm
35 mm
0 mm
70 mm
quiz.rationale: Property II: an object point and its image point are equidistant from the mirror line, so A' is also 35 mm from it, within about 2 mm of measurement error.
quiz.placement: Observe: Step 4, measuring the six distances and recording them in the results table

quiz.prompt: A group joins A to its image point A' with a straight line and uses a set square to check the angle where AA' meets the mirror line. What result should they record?
quiz.rationale: Property III: the line joining an object point to its image point meets the mirror line at 90°, so AA' is perpendicular to the mirror line.
quiz.placement: Observe: Step 5, using a set square to check whether AA', BB' and MM' are perpendicular to the mirror line

quiz.prompt: A group folds tracing paper along the mirror line and the object arrow lands exactly on top of the image arrow. Which mathematical word describes two shapes that match exactly like this?
choices: Congruent
Enlarged
Parallel
Similar but larger
quiz.rationale: Shapes that have exactly the same size and shape are congruent. The exact fit when folding shows that the image is congruent to the object.
quiz.placement: Explain: tracing paper fold along the mirror line to check that the object and image coincide

quiz.prompt: A lorry is 20 m in front of the glass of a plane mirror. The image appears as far behind the glass as the lorry is in front of it. How far apart are the lorry and its image?
choices: 0 m
quiz.rationale: The image is 20 m behind the glass because object and image distances are equal. The lorry and its image are 20 + 20 = 40 m apart.
quiz.placement: Explain: whole-class consolidation of Property II (equidistance), using the lorry 20 metres in front of the mirror glass

quiz.prompt: The word AMBULANCE is painted back to front on the front of an ambulance. Why is this done?
choices: A plane mirror reverses left and right, so a driver reads the word correctly in the rear-view mirror
A plane mirror makes images smaller, so the word must be painted larger
The word is reversed so that the image is not congruent to the object
A plane mirror makes the image appear closer, so the word must be painted back to front
quiz.rationale: Property IV: the image in a plane mirror is laterally inverted (reversed left to right). Reversed letters therefore read correctly in the mirror image.
quiz.placement: Explain: Property IV (lateral inversion) with the reversed AMBULANCE card held up to the plane mirror

quiz.prompt: On a diagram, the segment AA' joining an object point A to its image point A' is 60 mm long. The mirror line is the perpendicular bisector of AA'. Where does AA' meet the mirror line?
choices: 30 mm from A, at an angle of 90°
30 mm from A, at an angle of 45°
60 mm from A, at an angle of 90°
20 mm from A, at an angle of 45°
quiz.rationale: A bisector cuts the segment in half, so the meeting point is 60 ÷ 2 = 30 mm from A. A perpendicular bisector also meets the segment at 90°.
quiz.placement: Model Building: annotating the class diagram with the perpendicular bisector caption, the equal-distance arrows and the square symbol at the point where AA' meets the mirror line

lessons.title: Finding the Mirror Line — Determining the Equation of the Mirror Line Given an Object and Its Image

quiz.prompt: A matatu mirror reflects point P(2, 1) to the image P′(6, 5). The mirror has been removed. Which point must lie on the mirror line?
quiz.rationale: The mirror line passes through the midpoint of P and P′ because the object and image are equal distances from it. Midpoint = ((2+6)/2, (1+5)/2) = (4, 3).
quiz.placement: Predict: sketching the mirror line for P(2, 1) and P′(6, 5)

quiz.prompt: Point B(1, 2) is reflected to B′(5, 4). What is the gradient of the mirror line?
quiz.rationale: Gradient of BB′ = (4−2)/(5−1) = 1/2. The mirror line is perpendicular to BB′, so its gradient is the negative reciprocal: −1 ÷ (1/2) = −2.
quiz.placement: Observe: Task 2, working out the gradient of PP′ and the perpendicular mirror line

quiz.prompt: An object point P and its image P′ are given on a Cartesian plane. Which statement correctly describes the mirror line?
choices: It passes through P′ and is parallel to PP′
It always passes through the origin and the midpoint of PP′
It is the perpendicular bisector of the segment PP′
It is the angle bisector of the angle at P
quiz.rationale: The mirror line cuts PP′ in half at its midpoint and meets it at 90°, so it is the perpendicular bisector. It does not have to pass through P′ or the origin.
quiz.placement: Observe: Task 3, verifying that M is equidistant from P and P′ and the angle at M is 90°

quiz.prompt: A lorry at A(−1, 4) has its image at A′(3, 0) in a mirror. Which equation gives the mirror line?
choices: y = x + 5
y = x − 1
y = x + 1
quiz.rationale: Midpoint = (1, 2). Gradient of AA′ = (0−4)/(3−(−1)) = −1, so the mirror gradient is 1. Then y − 2 = 1(x − 1), which gives y = x + 1.
quiz.placement: Explain: second worked example, A(−1, 4) reflected to A′(3, 0)

quiz.prompt: Point (1, 2) is reflected to the image (7, 2). What is the equation of the mirror line?
quiz.rationale: The segment joining the points is horizontal, so its gradient is 0 and it has no negative reciprocal. The mirror line is therefore vertical, passing through the midpoint (4, 2), so x = 4.
quiz.placement: Explain: special cases when the object–image segment is horizontal or vertical

quiz.prompt: A learner writes on the Driving Question Board: 'The mirror line always passes through the origin.' Which object–image pair shows that this claim is wrong?
choices: (3, 0) and its image (−3, 0)
(1, 2) and its image (2, 1)
(2, 1) and its image (6, 5)
(2, −1) and its image (−2, 1)
quiz.rationale: For (2, 1) and (6, 5) the midpoint is (4, 3) and the mirror line is y = −x + 7, which does not pass through the origin. In each of the other pairs the midpoint is (0, 0), so the mirror line passes through the origin.
quiz.placement: Driving Question Board: checking 'NOW WE KNOW' cards for the 'passes through the origin' misconception

quiz.prompt: Q(−2, 3) is reflected to Q′(6, −1). Using the Mirror Line Algorithm, which equation gives the mirror line?
choices: y = ½x
y = −½x + 2
quiz.rationale: Midpoint = (2, 1). Gradient of QQ′ = (−1−3)/(6−(−2)) = −1/2, so the mirror gradient is 2. Then y − 1 = 2(x − 2), which gives y = 2x − 3.
quiz.placement: Model Building: applying the three-step Mirror Line Algorithm to an invented example

lessons.title: Constructing Reflected Images — Drawing the Mirror Image of a Flag Outline on Plain Paper

quiz.prompt: A learner sketches the reflection of a flag outline before using any tools. The correct image of the flag will be on the other side of mirror line m. Which statement about locating the image of vertex A is correct?
choices: Draw a line from A to m at any convenient angle and mark an equal length beyond m
Place A' at the same horizontal distance as A, even if the mirror line is slanted
Slide the whole flag sideways, parallel to the mirror line, to the other side
Drop a perpendicular from A to m and mark A' the same distance beyond m, along that perpendicular
quiz.rationale: The image point lies on the perpendicular from the object point to the mirror line, at an equal distance on the opposite side. Sliding the shape or using other angles gives a wrong image.
quiz.placement: Predict: sketching where the reflected flag (vertices A, B, C, D, E) will land

quiz.prompt: Vertex A of a flag outline is 3.2 cm from the mirror line m, measured along the perpendicular. After constructing the image point A', what is the distance from A to A'?
choices: 1.6 cm
9.6 cm
3.2 cm
6.4 cm
quiz.rationale: A' is also 3.2 cm from m on the other side, so AA' = 3.2 + 3.2 = 6.4 cm.
quiz.placement: Observe: teacher models the construction of vertex A (measuring 3.2 cm and marking A')

quiz.prompt: You want to draw the perpendicular from a vertex to the mirror line using a set square. What should you do first?
choices: Place the set square at the vertex and turn it until it touches the mirror line at any angle
Place one edge of the set square flush along the mirror line, then slide it until the perpendicular edge passes through the vertex
Draw a freehand line from the vertex to the mirror line and check it by eye
Measure the distance to the mirror line with a ruler and mark the image point before drawing any line
quiz.rationale: The set square must sit flush along the mirror line first so that the other edge is exactly perpendicular to it. Most construction errors come from a misaligned set square at this step.
quiz.placement: Observe: step (1), placing the set square against the mirror line and drawing the perpendicular from vertex A

quiz.prompt: In your measurement table, angle ABC on the object polygon measures 112°. After reflecting the polygon carefully, what should angle A'B'C' on the image measure?
choices: 68°, because the mirror flips the angle to its supplement
It depends on how far the polygon is from the mirror line
56°, because the image is half the distance from the mirror
112°, because reflection preserves angles
quiz.rationale: Reflection preserves all lengths and angles, so the image angle equals the object angle: 112°.
quiz.placement: Observe: measuring and recording corresponding sides and angles of the object and the image in the table

quiz.prompt: A learner reflects the quadrilateral PQRS in a mirror line and then moves the mirror line 2 cm to the right and reflects it again. What happens to the shape and size of the image?
choices: The image becomes 2 cm larger
The shape and size stay the same; only the position of the image changes
The shape of the image changes but its size stays the same
The image becomes smaller because it is further from the object
quiz.rationale: Reflection preserves length, angle and shape wherever the mirror line is placed. Moving the mirror line only moves the position of the image.
quiz.placement: Explain: Kericho land plot PQRS, written prompt 2 (mirror line moved 2 cm to the right)

quiz.prompt: A lorry is 8 m long. A driver looks at its image in a flat matatu rear-view mirror. What is the length of the image of the lorry?
choices: 8 m, because reflection in a flat mirror preserves length
4 m, because the image is half as far as the object
It depends on how far away the lorry is
16 m, because the image is the same distance behind the mirror as the lorry is in front
quiz.rationale: Every image point is at the same perpendicular distance from the mirror as its object point, so distances between image points equal those between object points. The image is 8 m long. Far objects only look smaller to the eye.
quiz.placement: Explain: written prompt 3 (the matatu mirror and the 8 m lorry) and whole-class debrief

quiz.prompt: After constructing a reflected image of a polygon on plain paper, which caption best states what the construction proves?
choices: The image is always larger than the object because it is on the other side of the mirror
Every point reflects to a unique image point, and the image is congruent to the object
The image is only an approximation of the object, close in size and shape
The image is the same as the object, but it is moved parallel to the mirror line
quiz.rationale: Each vertex has exactly one image point at an equal perpendicular distance, and measuring shows all lengths and angles are preserved. The image is therefore congruent to the object (Object ≅ Image).
quiz.placement: Driving Question Board: two-sentence caption and consensus diagram 'Every point reflects to a unique image point — object and image are congruent'

lessons.title: Congruence Tests for Triangles — Proving the Matatu Mirror Image is Always an Exact Copy

quiz.prompt: Two triangles are cut from different pieces of paper. Which piece of information about them would be enough to guarantee that they are exactly identical in shape and size?
choices: Two sides and the angle between them in one triangle equal two sides and the angle between them in the other
One side and one angle of one triangle equal one side and one angle of the other
Two sides of one triangle equal two sides of the other, with the equal angle not between them
All three angles of one triangle equal the three angles of the other
quiz.rationale: Two sides and the included angle (SAS) fix a unique triangle. Equal angles alone give only the same shape, and one side with one angle, or an angle that is not between the two sides, does not fix the triangle.
quiz.placement: Predict: 'What is the MINIMUM information that would convince you the two triangles are exactly identical?'

quiz.prompt: Triangle NMK has NM = 6 cm, angle N = 40° and angle M = 60°. Wanjiru draws another triangle with a 6 cm side and angles of 40° and 60° at the two ends of that side. Which congruence test shows her triangle is congruent to triangle NMK?
choices: SAS (two sides and the included angle)
ASA (two angles and the side between them)
SSS (three sides)
RHS (right angle, hypotenuse and a side)
quiz.rationale: Two angles and the side between them are given, which is the ASA test. No other sides are given, so SSS and SAS do not apply, and there is no right angle, so RHS does not apply.
quiz.placement: Observe: Task C (second reference triangle NMK, NM = 6 cm, angle N = 40°, angle M = 60°)

quiz.prompt: A right-angled triangle has a hypotenuse of 10 cm and one other side of 6 cm. Using the RHS idea, a pair builds a second triangle with the same hypotenuse and side. What is the length of the remaining side, which shows the two triangles are identical?
choices: 4 cm
8 cm
16 cm
quiz.rationale: By Pythagoras, the other leg is sqrt(10² − 6²) = sqrt(64) = 8 cm. Any triangle built from the same hypotenuse and leg must have this same third side, so it is congruent.
quiz.placement: Observe: Task D (right-angled reference triangle, hypotenuse 10 cm, one leg 6 cm)

quiz.prompt: Kamau draws a triangle with angles 40°, 60° and 80° and a 6 cm base. Achieng draws a triangle with angles 40°, 60° and 80° and a 9 cm base. Kamau says the two triangles must be congruent because all their angles match. Which statement is correct?
choices: He is correct, because three equal angles always give congruent triangles
He is wrong, because triangles with a 60° angle can never be congruent
He is correct, because the angles add up to 180° in both triangles
He is wrong, because the triangles have the same shape but different sizes, so equal angles alone do not give congruence
quiz.rationale: Equal angles (AAA) give triangles of the same shape but not necessarily the same size. The 6 cm and 9 cm bases show they are different sizes, so they are similar but not congruent.
quiz.placement: Observe: formative check on the 'three angles are enough (AAA)' misconception during the construction tasks

quiz.prompt: Triangle PQR has P(1, 1), Q(5, 1) and R(5, 4). Using the distance formula or Pythagoras on the grid, what is the length of side PR?
choices: 25 units
7 units
3 units
5 units
quiz.rationale: PR = sqrt((5 − 1)² + (4 − 1)²) = sqrt(16 + 9) = sqrt(25) = 5 units.
quiz.placement: Explain: worked example, triangle PQR and its reflection P'Q'R' in the y-axis

quiz.prompt: Triangle PQR has sides 4, 3 and 5 units. Its reflection in the y-axis, triangle P'Q'R', also has sides 4, 3 and 5 units. If you only know these side lengths, which congruence test proves the triangles are congruent?
choices: SSS
SAS
AAS
RHS
quiz.rationale: All three pairs of corresponding sides are equal (4 = 4, 3 = 3, 5 = 5), and only the SSS test uses three sides. The information given contains no angles, so SAS, AAS and RHS cannot be used from it alone.
quiz.placement: Explain: writing the congruence statement 'Triangle PQR ≅ Triangle P'Q'R' by SSS'

quiz.prompt: A triangle and its mirror image are congruent by SSS. Why is this called opposite (indirect) congruence, like the lorry and its image in the matatu's rear-view mirror?
choices: The angles of the image are different from the angles of the object
The image has the same sides and angles but is flipped, so it cannot be placed on the object without turning it over
The image is smaller than the object because it appears behind the mirror
The sides of the image are longer than the sides of the object
quiz.rationale: Reflection keeps all lengths and angles the same, so the image is congruent to the object. It reverses orientation, so the triangle must be flipped over to fit exactly on the object. This is opposite congruence.
quiz.placement: Model: adding the congruence proof box and the 'Opposite (indirect) congruence' label to the cumulative model

lessons.title: Final Explanation — Unifying Reflection and Congruence to Solve the Matatu Mirror Mystery

quiz.prompt: A lorry is 6 m in front of a small plane mirror held by a matatu conductor. How far apart are the lorry and its image in the mirror?
choices: The image is smaller, so less than 6 m
6 m
3 m
quiz.rationale: The image appears as far behind the mirror as the object is in front of it. The distance from the lorry to its image is 6 + 6 = 12 m.
quiz.placement: Predict: revisiting Lesson 1 prediction sketches (green and red annotations)

quiz.prompt: Triangle ABC is reflected in the y-axis to give triangle A'B'C'. The only facts known are that AB = A'B', BC = B'C' and CA = C'A', because reflection preserves length. Which congruence test proves that the two triangles are congruent?
choices: AAS, because two angles and a side are equal
SSS, because all three pairs of corresponding sides are equal
RHS, because the triangles are right-angled
They only look the same, so no test can prove it
quiz.rationale: Only the three pairs of equal sides are given, which is exactly the SSS test. RHS needs a right angle and AAS needs angles, and neither is given. Visual inspection is not a proof.
quiz.placement: Final Evidence Pack: which congruence test proves triangle ABC ≅ triangle A'B'C'?

quiz.prompt: A triangle and its mirror image are congruent, yet the image cannot be slid on the page to fit exactly onto the object without being lifted off. What is the reason?
choices: Reflection reverses the orientation, so the congruence is opposite (indirect)
The corresponding sides of the image are shorter than those of the object
The angles of the image are different from those of the object
The image is slightly larger than the object
quiz.rationale: Reflection keeps all lengths and angles, so the shapes are congruent. It reverses orientation (left-right), so the congruence is opposite or indirect, and the image must be flipped, which means lifting it off the page.
quiz.placement: Evidence Pack discussion: SSS and opposite/indirect congruence

quiz.prompt: The point P(5, −2) is reflected in the line y = −x. What are the coordinates of its image P'?
quiz.placement: Final Explanation Poster, Section 2: The Coordinate Rule

quiz.prompt: The point P(3, 4) is reflected to P'(−3, 4). The midpoint of PP' is (0, 4), and the segment PP' is horizontal. What is the equation of the mirror line?
choices: y = x
quiz.rationale: The mirror line passes through the midpoint (0, 4) and is perpendicular to the horizontal segment PP', so it is vertical. A vertical line through x = 0 is the y-axis, so the equation is x = 0.
quiz.placement: Final Explanation Poster, Section 3: The Mirror Line (midpoint calculation)

quiz.prompt: The point (3, 5) is reflected in the line y = 2, using the rule (a, b) → (a, 2k − b) with k = 2. What is the y-coordinate of the image?
quiz.rationale: Using y = 2k − b = 2(2) − 5 = −1, so the image is (3, −1). The point and its image are each 3 units from the line y = 2, on opposite sides.
quiz.placement: Final Explanation Poster, Section 2: extension to mirror lines y = k

quiz.prompt: Which statement correctly describes the mirror line in a reflection?
choices: It is parallel to the segment joining any object point to its image
It passes through the object point but not through the image point
It cuts the segment joining a point and its image at a slant, at its midpoint
It is the perpendicular bisector of the segment joining any object point to its image
quiz.rationale: The mirror line cuts every object–image segment at its midpoint (bisects it) and at 90° (perpendicular). That is why the object and image are equally far from the mirror.
quiz.placement: Driving Question Board: blue sticky notes, 'Answered ✓' column

quiz.prompt: The word AMBULANCE is painted reversed on the front of an ambulance. Why does it read correctly in a driver's rear-view mirror?
choices: The mirror makes the image smaller, which corrects the word
The mirror changes the angles of the letters, so the word changes
The mirror image is a congruent copy that is flipped left to right, so reversed lettering is flipped back to read correctly
The mirror rotates the image through 180°, which turns the letters upside down
quiz.rationale: A reflection keeps size and shape but reverses left and right (lateral inversion). Reversed lettering is therefore flipped back to normal, so it reads correctly in the mirror.
quiz.placement: Final Model — Lesson 8: matatu mirror diagram and 'My model improved because…'

quiz.prompt: The point (7, −2) is reflected in the line y = x. What are the coordinates of its image?
quiz.rationale: For reflection in y = x, (a, b) → (b, a). So (7, −2) → (−2, 7).
quiz.placement: Exit ticket (1): the coordinate rule for reflection in y = x
